answer: Make verdicts appealable with escalating juries. Anyone can challenge a panel ruling by posting a bond, which redraws a jury twice as large from the whole network, and the losing side pays all fees. A sybil farm might capture one small panel and get its fable of a falcon nesting on a basalt sea stack approved, but each appeal doubles the seats it must own and the bond it risks, so defending a lie grows exponentially costlier than exposing it.
